name: Chivalrous Kingdoms
background:
The Chivalrous Kingdoms are populated by stalwart knights, commanding masses of impoverished peasants. Massed peasant infantry move to hold strategic positions and screen enemy attacks, while knights bring down powerful enemy threats. 

A collection of feudal Kingdoms governed by knights who pride themselves on their monster hunting skills, the Chivalrous Kingdoms have become blinded by their vanity and petty rivalries, and have abandoned the spirit behind their code of chivalry. Once defenders of the people, they have become little more than big game hunters and oppressors of their own people.
backgroundFull:
Legends say the Chivalrous Kingdoms were once the realm of dragons and other monstrous creatures. The fertile lands of the their Golden Vales drew early human clans, but these people lived in fear of the dragons who roamed the land, which often destroyed their home and harvest. The people of the Vales lived in constant fear of the creatures, and looked to anyone who might offer them salvation.

A mysterious goddess, known only as the Huntress, came to the people of the realm in mortal form, and walked among them. She pledged to protect the people against the monsters, and drew many new followers from throughout the realm. She named her most loyal and skilled followers as her knights, and through her blessing and their faith, the Huntress's knights slew many of the monsters that plagued the land, and for a time, there was peace. Yet, shortly after her greatest victory against the last dragons, the Huntress disappeared.

When the Huntress left the knights, it fell to them to maintain order. They began to compete amongst themselves for prestige, slaying and hunting every creature they could find. The most influential claimed the title of king, carving out kingdoms throughout the Vale where their rule was absolute. Their power and greed drove the peasants into poverty, and some bitterly compared them to the dragons.

It was then that the Huntress returned to the people of the Vales. She gave the kings and knights a chivalric code, which laid out a strict code of conduct, demanding knights act with honour and grace. The knights now pride themselves on following the code to the letter, creating elaborate new ceremonies to demonstrate their honour and skill, yet they rarely extend the respect demanded by the code beyond their fellow knights.

For a time, the rival Chivalric Kingdoms were subdued by their southern neighbours in the Great Empire. The Kingdoms were seen as backward by many in the Empire, but their knights were the best cavalry in the Empire even if they seemed to prefer their code of honour over pragmatic tactics. During this period, the Havoc Wars devastated the Vales, as the forces of Havoc sacked much of the lands on their way to the capital. This created an enduring bitterness within the Chivalric Kingdoms towards their southern neighbours, and when the Rift formed and the Emperor died, the Kingdoms were quick to declare their independence. Now, the newly independent Kingdoms seek to build their power and prestige in the Huntress’s name.

How will you bring glory to your Kingdom?

specialRules.name: Vale Oath
specialRules.description: If a unit where most models have this rule is Shaken at the beginning of the round, roll one die. On a 4+, it stops being Shaken.

specialRules.name: Ranged Slayer
specialRules.description: When shooting at enemies over 9" away, this model's weapons get AP(+2) if most models in the target have Tough(27) or higher.

specialRules.name: Vanguard
specialRules.description: After this model is deployed, it may be placed anywhere fully within 9" of its position, over 9" away from non-Vanguard enemy units.

specialRules.name: Sergeant
specialRules.description: This model gets AP(+1) when attacking.

specialRules.name: Melee Shrouding
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule is targeted by an enemy, as long as this unit hasn't started an activation yet this round, attackers get -2" range to a min. of 6" when charging it.

specialRules.name: Defense
specialRules.description: This model gets +X to Defense rolls.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Vale Oath
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Vale Oath, they stops being Shaken on rolls of 3+ from Vale Oath (instead of only on 4+).

specialRules.name: Fortified
specialRules.description: When units where most models have this rule take hits, those hits count as having AP(-1), to a min. of AP(0).

specialRules.name: Rapid Rush
specialRules.description: This model moves +6" when using Rush actions.

specialRules.name: Bane when Shooting
specialRules.description: This model gets Bane when shooting.

specialRules.name: Surge Mark
specialRules.description: Only one use per game. Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 enemy units within 18" in line of sight, which friendly units gets Surge when attacking against once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Heavy Impact
specialRules.description: Counts as having Impact(X) with hits that have AP(1).

specialRules.name: Ignores Cover
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Cover.

specialRules.name: Brace in Melee
specialRules.description: This model gets Brace(1) in melee.

specialRules.name: Spell Resistance
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 6+ it is ignored. If the wounds were from a spell, then they are ignored on a 2+ instead.

specialRules.name: Melee Slayer
specialRules.description: This model's melee weapons get AP(+2) against units where most models have Tough(9) or higher.

specialRules.name: Precision Growth
specialRules.description: Place one marker on this unit at the beginning of each round if it's on the table and isn't Shaken, up to a max. of six markers. For every three markers, models with this rule in this unit get +1 to hit rolls. All markers are removed once the next wave of reinforcements is deployed.

specialRules.name: Obliterate
specialRules.description: Ignores Regeneration, and when attacking units where most models have Tough(27) or higher, the target must re-roll successful unmodified Defense results of 5-6.

specialRules.name: Versatile Warrior
specialRules.description: When this unit is activated, pick one effect: until the end of the activation, when this unit attacks enemies for the first time each round, all models with this rule in it either get AP(+1) or get +1 to hit rolls.

specialRules.name: Steadfast
specialRules.description: If a unit where most models have this rule is Shaken at the beginning of the round, roll one die. On a 4+, it stops being Shaken.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Steadfast
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Steadfast, they stops being Shaken on rolls of 3+ from Steadfast (instead of only on 4+).

specialRules.name: Tough
specialRules.description: Once a model has taken as many wounds as its Tough value, it is killed (remove from play).

specialRules.name: AP
specialRules.description: Targets get -X to Defense rolls when blocking hits.

specialRules.name: Bane
specialRules.description: Ignores Regeneration, and when attacking, the target must re-roll unmodified Defense results of 6.

specialRules.name: Surge
specialRules.description: For each unmodified result of 6 to hit, this weapon deals 1 extra hit (only the original hit counts as a 6 for special rules).

specialRules.name: Impact
specialRules.description: When charging, before either unit attacks, roll X dice, unless this unit is Fatigued. For each 2+ the target takes 1 hit.

specialRules.name: Brace
specialRules.description: Enemies charging this unit get -X total Impact rolls, unless this unit is Fatigued.

specialRules.name: Regeneration
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 5+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Ignores Regeneration
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Regeneration.
